blocks.text:
## Four sides of Brazil in one journey

In Rio, the programme includes Sugarloaf and Corcovado with an English-speaking guide. From Sugarloaf, you can see Copacabana, Guanabara Bay, the islands and Christ the Redeemer. At Corcovado, travel through Tijuca Forest to the statue and the panorama over the city.

At Iguazu, city views give way to waterfalls and rainforest. Explore the Brazilian side of the national park along the paths towards the Devil’s Throat. The programme continues with the Macuco Safari boat ride close to the falls and a visit to the Bird Park.

The Pantanal is a flat region where water shapes the landscape. During the rainy season, parts of the plains flood; during the dry season, lakes, channels and grasslands remain. Herons and storks may be seen along the banks, caimans in the water, and parrots and toucans in the branches. At Pousada Aguapé, the lodge plans activities according to the weather and season, including horse riding, wildlife walks, piranha fishing and caiman spotting. Full board and lodge excursions are included.

Búzios ends the journey with 3 nights by the ocean. Beaches on the eastern side of the peninsula are windier and cooler, while those to the west have calmer, warmer water. You can choose diving, walking, a schooner trip or a buggy ride, or simply spend your days on different beaches.

The route moves between distinct settings. During the first 3 days, discover Rio from above and from its historic districts. The city then gives way to waterfalls, with the sound and movement of water. In the Pantanal, your attention shifts to animals, birds and open spaces. The final 3 nights let you slow down beside the ocean.

There is room to choose additional activities. In Rio, options after the main tours include Lapa at night, the old town, tropical islands, Petrópolis, Rocinha, the Botanical Garden, an evening show and a helicopter flight. In Búzios, you can plan your free days around the sea and beaches.
